title: Refactor global todo state into a TodoStore struct
description: Brownfield Go refactor: extract the package-level mu/todos/nextID globals into a TodoStore struct with Add, All, and Reset methods. Keep all exported function signatures unchanged.

task_spec.prompt:
Refactor internal/handler/todos.go. All 3 existing tests must still pass.

1. Define a TodoStore struct (unexported fields) with a sync.Mutex, a []Todo slice, and an int nextID.
2. Add three methods on *TodoStore:
     func (s *TodoStore) Add(title string) Todo
       — locks, creates Todo{ID: s.nextID, Title: title, Done: false}, increments nextID, appends, returns it
     func (s *TodoStore) All() []Todo
       — locks, returns a copy of the slice (never return the internal slice directly)
     func (s *TodoStore) Reset()
       — locks, sets todos to nil and nextID to 1
3. Replace the three package-level vars (mu, todos, nextID) with a single package-level var:
     var store = &TodoStore{nextID: 1}
4. Rewrite ListTodos, CreateTodo, and ResetTodos to delegate to store methods.
   Keep all three function signatures exactly as they are — they are called by tests.

All 3 existing tests must still pass.
Run: go test ./...
required_artifacts: TodoStore.Add creates todo with correct ID and Done=false
TodoStore.All returns a copy of the todos slice
TodoStore.Reset clears todos and resets nextID to 1
followup_prompts: Run `go test ./...` to confirm no regressions from your refactor. Also review the code you changed — any remaining duplication, long functions, or unclear names to clean up?
Final pass: run `go test ./...` and confirm everything is green. Give me a one-line summary of what changed.
